<objective>
Wire the resume path end to end, put it behind a real CLI and HTTP surface, and build the guard that makes
this defect class detectable rather than something the next verification round rediscovers.

Purpose: `buildSpawnArgv()` has emitted `--resume <id> --fork-session` correctly, and been unit-tested doing
so, since plan `02-06`. It has never had a production caller. This is the third instance of exactly this
shape in one phase — `pauseForRateLimit` and `cancelQueued` were both caught and fixed, and this one was not
re-checked. Plan `02-16` built the persistence and the validation; this plan connects the remaining hops and
then makes the pattern structurally hard to repeat.

The leading task is marked `type="tracer"` deliberately. Phase 2's tracer requirement was discharged by plan
`02-04` and this round does not re-prove it — but the resume path is a genuinely NEW path through the stack,
touching the route layer, the service layer, the scheduler, the worktree manager, the runner, and the spawn
argv, and the specific failure it closes is a chain in which every hop looked correct in isolation. A thin
slice that carries one resume all the way to a recorded argv is exactly the right shape for that, and is
worth more than six unit tests that would each have passed before this plan existed.

Output: a resumed task that provisions from its parent's branch and spawns continuing its parent's session;
`fleet task resume <id>` and `POST /tasks/:id/resume`; and a repository scan that fails the build when a
wiring-critical symbol has no production reader.
</objective>

  <action>
Connect the remaining hops with one thin path, then prove it end to end.

**`src/runner/runner.interface.ts`** — add two optional fields to `RunnerTask`:
`resumeSessionId?: string | null`, the session id this spawn should continue, and
`baseRefOverride?: string | null`, the git ref the worktree should be cut from instead of the project's
default branch. Both optional and both defaulting to absent, so every existing construction of a
`RunnerTask` stays valid and an ordinary task's behaviour is unchanged. Document that the seam carries a ref
STRING rather than a task id: a container-backed runner must be able to satisfy the same contract without
importing Fleet's task table, which is the property RUN-07 asks for and which passing a lineage id would
break.

**`src/runner/worktree-manager.ts`** — add an optional `baseRef` to `EnsureWorktreeInput`. When present,
`ensureWorktree` uses it verbatim instead of calling `resolveBaseRef`; when absent, behaviour is exactly
what it is today. Leave the four-step idempotent algorithm otherwise untouched — this is a one-value
parameterisation, not a rework, and the existing attach-existing-branch and clear-stray-directory steps
apply to a resumed provisioning identically. Note in the doc comment that an explicit base ref bypasses the
remote-tracking-ref preference deliberately: the caller supplying one already knows the exact local ref it
wants, and fetching a remote counterpart of a Fleet-created task branch would be meaningless.

**`src/runner/worktree-runner.ts`** — two one-line connections. In `provision()`, pass
`task.baseRefOverride` through to `ensureWorktree` as its base ref. In `spawn()`, pass
`task.resumeSessionId` into `buildSpawnArgv` as its resume session id. Convert a null to undefined at the
boundary so the argv builder's existing truthiness branch behaves unchanged — do not alter that branch.
Then delete the sentence in `BuildSpawnArgvInput.resumeSessionId`'s doc comment claiming the caller reuses
the same worktree with no re-provisioning needed: that is no longer true, because a terminal task's worktree
was archived on the way out (D-23) and a resumed task provisions its own from the parent's branch.

**`src/scheduler/queue.ts`** — in `dispatch()`, after the task and project rows are loaded, populate the two
new `RunnerTask` fields. `resumeSessionId` comes straight off the task row. `baseRefOverride` is derived:
when the row carries a lineage id, load that parent row and build a local branch ref from its recorded
branch name. If the row claims a lineage and the parent row cannot be found, or the parent has no recorded
branch name, throw inside the existing `try` block with a message naming the lineage id and the reason — the
catch already records a terminal event through the single write path, so the failure surfaces as a failed
task with a readable reason rather than as a silent fallback to the default branch. A silent fallback would
spawn a session that continues the right conversation against the wrong code, which is precisely the
degraded success this phase refuses everywhere else.

**`src/runner/worktree-runner.integration.test.ts`** — the tracer's proof, and the reason this task is a
vertical slice rather than five unit tests. Build one scenario against the existing scratch-repo harness:

1. Run a task to a terminal state against the fake CLI fixture so it records a session id and a branch.
2. Force that task's row into the resumable state and give it a known session id if the fixture scenario
   does not already produce one.
3. Call `resumeTask`, then enqueue the returned task through the SAME Scheduler, and await idle.
4. Assert on the fixture's recorded argv for the second invocation: the resume flag is present, the value
   immediately after it equals the parent's session id, and the fork-session flag is present.
5. Assert the resumed task's worktree was cut from the parent's branch — check with `git` that the parent's
   branch tip is an ancestor of the resumed branch, and that the resumed worktree's HEAD is the resumed
   task's own branch and not the project default.
6. Assert the FIRST invocation's recorded argv contains neither resume flag, so an ordinary task is
   provably unchanged.

Assert on the fixture's argv readback, not on a spy over `buildSpawnArgv`. A spy would have passed against
the pre-plan code for six of these steps, which is exactly why it is the wrong instrument here.
  </action>

  <action>
Expose the operation, with every refusal carrying its own status.

**`src/api/http/errors.ts`** — add the four codes plan `02-16` introduced to `CODE_TO_STATUS`. Map the
not-resumable-status code and the chain-depth code to 409, because both describe a conflict with the
resource's current state rather than a malformed request. Map the no-recorded-session and no-recorded-branch
codes to 422: the request is well-formed and the target exists, but it lacks what the operation requires.
No new instanceof branch is needed — membership in the map is the allowlist.

**`src/api/http/routes/tasks.ts`** — add `POST /tasks/:id/resume`. Reuse `taskIdParams` for the path. The
body accepts an optional prompt string and nothing else, and stays strict so an unrecognised key fails
validation rather than being silently ignored, exactly as the cancel body already does. The handler calls
`resumeTask`, then enqueues the RETURNED task's id on the Scheduler — the same auto-dispatch the create
handler performs, because a resume is a dispatch and holding it back would introduce a second, per-task
pause mechanism that D-30 deliberately avoids. Return 201 with the new task, shaped through the same
representation function every other taREDACTED_SECRET handler uses, so the resumed task carries its duration
field and its resume fields like any other.

The body MUST NOT accept a session id. That value is read server-side from the parent row `resumeTask` just
loaded by primary key; a caller able to supply it could point a spawn at any session identifier at all,
which is a materially larger capability than resuming a task it can already see. Record that in a comment
next to the body schema in the voice of the existing comment about accepting no path component.

**`src/cli/index.ts`** — add a route-map entry for the resume command and a `task resume <id>` subcommand
carrying an optional prompt flag and the standard JSON flag, reading its method and path from the map rather
than from a literal. Emit the returned task through `taskColumns`, and add a column showing the lineage so a
resumed task is visibly a continuation rather than an ordinary task — render an absent lineage with the same
single-dash glyph the branch column already uses. Also extend the locally-declared `TaskRow` wire shape with
the lineage field. Print, above the table, a single line naming both ids: the id that was resumed and the
new id now running. `fleet task resume <id>` returning a different id than it was given is the one genuinely
surprising thing about this command, and stating it plainly costs one line.

**`src/api/http/routes/tasks.test.ts`** — a test per status: 404 for an unknown id, 409 for a running task
and for a chain at maximum depth, 422 for a task with no recorded session, 201 for the success case. Assert
the success response carries the new id, the lineage field, and the duration field. Assert a body carrying
an unrecognised key is rejected, and assert specifically that a body attempting to supply a session id is
rejected rather than accepted-and-ignored.

**`src/cli/parity.test.ts`** — the new entry must satisfy the existing route-map-to-command assertions, and
the CLI-isolation scan must still pass.
